method.cold_controls: One per policy and case, after the reuse runs.
method.priming: Clear prior compiler caches in private copies, prime A-to-B with the instrumented 32 MiB binary, then compare independent copies on A-to-C.
method.timing: CLI review wall time; no concurrent builds/tests. Helper preparation plus exclusive native subphases logged to stderr.
method.memory: os.wait4 command child ru_maxrss, macOS bytes; not simultaneous process-tree total.
method.equality: Whole packets within each case excluding only analysis_cache and tokens.

validation: 12 Go top-level tests passed, including cache invalidation, export/transport bounds, unchanged facts with timings on/off and recursive timer accounting.
Rust numeric timing-filter test passed via rustc --test on the exact function and test module extracted from go_types.rs.
20 end-to-end review packets equal within each case, with expected cache hits and token bounds.
limitations: Two samples per reuse arm and one cold control; older local archives, not the eight production probe PRs.
Only review timed; admission, collection, vendoring, cache priming, cloning and models excluded.
OS caches not flushed; unrelated machine activity uncontrolled. Cold controls vary materially despite no initial package cache, so the small total-time gain is not a robust production estimate.
Profiles/dependencies unchanged; full-pool loading with changed dependencies and reduced space for new exports was not evaluated.
Optional export rejection occurred in some runs and fell back to native checking; no packet drift.
Instrumentation changes the helper identity; a deployed instrumented build needs native caches to rebuild once.

decision.reason: Nexus shows a small local latency reduction at higher memory; platform-rbac does not benefit, cold controls vary, and changed-dependency workloads are untested.
decision.next_target: Amortize helper compilation across review calls using the existing process-local helper cache; profile/discuss package discovery next. Existing impact.report/graph.impact API can keep the process alive.
